Sadness can arise after an irreversible loss, separation, rejection, or when events are not what you wanted or expected.

## Words describing sadness

Agony, alienation, anguish, disappointment, disconnection, despair, distress, grief, homesickness, hurt, insecurity, loneliness, melancholy, misery, neglect, rejection, sorrow, suffering, unhappiness, and woe.

## Prompting events and interpretations

Events include death or permanent loss, separation, not getting what was wanted, rejection, isolation, helplessness, or another person's suffering. Interpretations may predict that separation will not end, needs will not be met, life is hopeless, or you are worthless.

## Body changes, expressions, and action urges

Low energy, heaviness, tears, chest or gut pain, difficulty swallowing, dizziness, lethargy, or breathlessness can occur. Actions and urges include crying, slowing down, withdrawing, avoiding, staying in bed, giving up, or speaking quietly.

## Aftereffects

Happy events may be hard to remember; irritation, yearning, negative outlook, self-blame, rumination, insomnia, or appetite changes can follow.

## When sadness fits the facts

Sadness fits when someone or something has been lost permanently, or events are not what you wanted and hoped they would be.

## Acting on the urge, Opposite Action, and Checking the Facts

When sadness fits, grieve, seek support, accept what cannot be changed, and problem-solve what can. When it does not fit or withdrawal is ineffective, get active, approach, avoid avoiding, build mastery, increase pleasant events, and attend to the present.
